You are a senior Chrome Extension engineer, product engineer, frontend architect, data/UI engineer, and UX designer.

We have already completed two major stages of this Chrome extension:

LEVEL 1:
Existing original extension functionality.

LEVEL 2:
A complete enhancement/reskin of the COMSATS Lahore SIS portal:

https://lhr-sis.comsats.edu.pk

The portal now has:
- a significantly improved modern UI
- dark mode
- improved navigation
- redesigned tables/forms/components
- reorganized information where useful
- dashboard improvements
- better visual hierarchy
- enhanced usability

The Level 2 implementation is working extremely well.

DO NOT rewrite or regress it.

We are now implementing:

# LEVEL 3 — COMPLETE STUDENT COMPANION

The goal is to evolve the extension beyond a portal reskin into a genuinely useful COMSATS Lahore student companion.

The finished product should make students think:

"This isn't just a better-looking SIS anymore. This is the tool I actually use to manage my university life."

The extension should intelligently combine:

1. Existing SIS information
2. Derived analytics
3. Academic calculators
4. Timetable intelligence
5. Attendance intelligence
6. GPA/CGPA planning
7. Empty-room discovery
8. Useful shortcuts
9. Context-aware tools
10. Quality-of-life functionality
11. Better presentation of existing portal data
12. New insights derived locally from data the student can already access

You have access to Chrome DevTools MCP.

I will manually log into SIS when necessary.

Use Chrome DevTools extensively to understand the real portal before designing Level 3.

DO NOT blindly implement a predetermined list of features.

First understand the portal completely.

Then design the student companion around the information and opportunities that actually exist.

---

# PHASE 1 — COMPLETE SIS RECONNAISSANCE

Before adding Level 3 features, systematically inspect the ENTIRE authenticated SIS portal.

Use Chrome DevTools MCP while I am logged in.

Do not inspect only the dashboard.

Navigate through every meaningful student-accessible page and understand the portal as a system.

Build an internal map of:

- all navigation items
- pages
- routes
- query parameters
- tabs
- forms
- tables
- semester selectors
- course selectors
- academic information
- timetable information
- attendance information
- results
- transcript
- GPA/CGPA
- course marks
- assessments
- quizzes
- assignments
- mids
- finals if shown
- teacher information
- course information
- fee information
- registration information
- exam-related information
- notices
- student profile
- degree information
- semester history
- credit-hour information
- any downloadable documents
- any useful information I have not explicitly listed

For every important page inspect:

1. Visible UI
2. DOM structure
3. Relevant selectors
4. Navigation behavior
5. Data represented
6. Whether the page reloads or updates dynamically
7. Whether data comes from initial HTML, XHR/fetch, forms, or another mechanism
8. Relationships between pages
9. Information that could be summarized elsewhere
10. Information from which useful student analytics could be derived

Use the Network panel when useful to understand how the portal itself loads its OWN data.

However:

DO NOT:
- steal credentials
- expose passwords
- export session cookies
- bypass authorization
- access another student's information
- abuse endpoints
- attempt privilege escalation
- modify university records
- fuzz private APIs

You are studying normal functionality available to the authenticated student account.

# PHASE 2 — STUDY COMSATS PLUS

Inspect:

https://www.comsatsplus.com

I specifically want you to investigate two features:

1. GPA / CGPA tools
2. Empty Room Finder

Use the public website through browser inspection, normal HTTP access, DevTools, its rendered UI, and publicly accessible resources where appropriate.

Understand the FUNCTIONAL BEHAVIOR of these tools.

Do not copy their branding, source code, proprietary assets or UI.

We are building our own implementation integrated into SIS.

Treat COMSATS Plus as:

REFERENCE / RESEARCH

not:

CODE TO COPY.

---

# FEATURE A — GPA / CGPA SYSTEM

COMSATS Plus currently provides academic tools including:

- GPA calculator
- CGPA calculator
- GPA planning / target CGPA calculator
- internal marks calculator

Study how these work.

But VERY IMPORTANT:

COMSATS Plus is NOT automatically the authoritative source for COMSATS academic policy.

Before implementing calculations, verify applicable grading rules against current OFFICIAL COMSATS University Islamabad / CUI academic policies, notifications, handbooks or other authoritative university sources.

Determine:

- grading scale
- grade-point mapping
- percentage boundaries
- credit-hour weighting
- GPA formula
- CGPA formula
- treatment of failures
- repeated courses if relevant
- theory/lab rules if relevant
- whether rules differ by admission batch
- whether grading policy has changed historically

The student's batch/admission semester may matter.

DO NOT hard-code one grading scheme without verifying whether SIS students can belong to different grading-policy cohorts.

Where appropriate create a centralized academic-policy configuration such as:

academicPolicy/
    current-policy.ts
    legacy-policy.ts
    grade-mapping.ts
    gpa.ts
    cgpa.ts

Use verified rules.

---

# BUILD A FIRST-CLASS ACADEMIC TOOLKIT

Do not merely create a tiny calculator popup.

Integrate GPA intelligence naturally into SIS.

Potential functionality:

## Semester GPA Calculator

Allow:

Course
Credit Hours
Grade or Marks

Automatically calculate:

- grade points
- honor/quality points
- semester GPA
- total semester credits

Where SIS already knows:

- registered courses
- course names
- credit hours

PREFILL THEM.

The student should not have to manually re-enter information that SIS already knows.

Example:

Current Semester GPA Calculator

Data structures & Algorithms    4 CH    [Grade ▼]
Operating Systems              4 CH    [Grade ▼]
Machine Learning               3 CH    [Grade ▼]
COAL                           4 CH    [Grade ▼]

Projected GPA: 3.47

---

# CGPA CALCULATOR

Where SIS exposes:

- existing CGPA
- completed credits
- previous semester information

prefill those values automatically where reliable.

Allow the student to calculate:

Current CGPA
+
Projected Semester GPA
=
Projected New CGPA

Display calculations transparently.

Do not hide assumptions.

---

# TARGET CGPA PLANNER

Create a planner such as:

Current CGPA:        3.24
Completed Credits:  74
Current Semester:   18 CH
Target CGPA:         3.40

Required Semester GPA:
3.98

Or:

Target is mathematically impossible within the selected credits.

Provide useful scenario analysis.

Examples:

Target 3.30 → required GPA 3.55
Target 3.40 → required GPA 3.98
Target 3.50 → not achievable this semester

Use correct credit-weighted mathematics.

---

# COURSE MARKS → GPA INTELLIGENCE

This is one of the most important Level 3 opportunities.

Inspect whether SIS exposes individual course marks such as:

- quizzes
- assignments
- lab work
- mids
- sessionals
- final examination
- obtained marks
- total marks
- aggregate marks

If enough reliable data exists, create contextual academic analysis.

Examples:

CURRENT COURSE PERFORMANCE

Machine Learning

Obtained so far:
43 / 50

Remaining:
50 marks

Current percentage:
86%

Possible final outcomes:

To finish with:
A   → approximately X required
A-  → approximately Y required
B+  → approximately Z required

ONLY perform this analysis when the underlying assessment structure and policy are known well enough to calculate it correctly.

Clearly distinguish:

ACTUAL SIS DATA

from

PROJECTED / ESTIMATED RESULT

Never present projections as official grades.

---

# "WHAT DO I NEED IN THE FINAL?" TOOL

If SIS exposes sufficient assessment data and weighting information, provide a tool where appropriate:

Current Marks: 42/50
Final Weight: 50%

Target:
A-

Required Final Performance:
approximately XX/50

Also allow custom targets.

This could become extremely useful during exams.

But calculations must be based on verified assessment structure.

If assessment weights vary by course, do not assume they are universal.

---

# GPA SCENARIO MODE

Allow students to experiment with grade combinations:

Algorithms      A-
Operating Sys   B+
ML              A
COAL            B

Projected SGPA:
3.xx

Projected CGPA:
3.xx

Changing one grade should immediately update projections.

Courses and credit hours should be automatically populated from SIS whenever possible.

---

# ACADEMIC HISTORY ANALYTICS

If semester history exists, consider creating useful analytics such as:

CGPA trend

Semester 1    3.10
Semester 2    3.27
Semester 3    3.35
Semester 4    3.41

Other useful summaries may include:

- highest semester GPA
- lowest semester GPA
- completed credit hours
- remaining credits if degree information permits
- grade distribution
- credit-weighted performance
- semester-over-semester change

Avoid useless analytics.

Everything should answer a question a student might genuinely have.

---

# FEATURE B — EMPTY ROOM FINDER

Inspect the COMSATS Plus Empty Room Finder carefully.

Determine how room availability is obtained.

Understand:

- room list
- timetable structure
- day selection
- time slots
- current-time handling
- buildings/blocks
- filtering
- availability determination
- data freshness
- whether availability is derived from a timetable dataset or a public endpoint
- how practical/lab rooms are represented
- how conflicts are handled

Do not blindly depend on undocumented third-party APIs if a more robust implementation can be built.

Prefer this hierarchy:

1. Official/public COMSATS data if available
2. Reliable timetable data that can be processed locally
3. Publicly accessible third-party data when appropriate and permitted

If COMSATS Plus computes availability from timetable data, reproduce the underlying concept independently rather than copying implementation code.

---

# EMPTY ROOM FINDER UX

Integrate it naturally into the enhanced SIS experience.

Potential entry points:

Dashboard:
"Find Empty Room"

Student Companion / Tools:
"Room Finder"

Timetable:
"Find free room during this gap"

Possible UI:

AVAILABLE NOW

Block A

A-2      Free until 11:30
A-5      Free until 12:30
A-7      Free until 10:00

Block B

B-3      Free
B-6      Occupied

Filters:

[Building]
[Floor]
[Room type]
[Available for at least]
[Time]
[Day]

Useful presets:

Available Now
Next Hour
For 2 Hours
At Custom Time

---

# SMART ROOM FINDER

Do more than simply list "Free / Occupied."

Where the underlying schedule permits, calculate:

Free until 12:30 PM

Next class:
Data Structures
12:30 – 2:00

or:

Free:
10:00 – 1:00

This makes the feature much more useful.

---

# TIMETABLE + ROOM FINDER INTEGRATION

If the SIS timetable exposes today's schedule, connect the two systems.

Example:

TODAY

09:00–10:30 Machine Learning
10:30–12:30 FREE
12:30–14:00 Operating Systems

During the 2-hour gap:

"Find study room"

→ automatically search rooms available from 10:30–12:30.

This is the kind of integration that makes this extension feel like a real student companion.

# PHASE 3 — INVENT OUR OWN LEVEL 3 FEATURES

The GPA system and Room Finder are mandatory.

But they should NOT be the entire Level 3.

After you understand every SIS page, independently identify high-value features we can build using existing student data.

Think like a COMSATS student.

Ask:

"What would save students time?"

"What do students repeatedly calculate manually?"

"What information is buried inside SIS?"

"What information requires too many clicks?"

"What information could be combined?"

"What questions can SIS data answer but the portal currently doesn't?"

"What small tools would students use every week?"

Implement genuinely useful opportunities you discover.

---

# POSSIBLE STUDENT COMPANION FEATURES

The following are IDEAS, not unconditional requirements.

Only implement them where actual SIS data supports them and where they improve the experience.

---

# 1. ATTENDANCE INTELLIGENCE

If attendance data exists, upgrade it significantly.

For every course potentially show:

Attendance
21 / 25
84%

Also derive useful information where mathematically valid.

Examples:

Classes you can currently miss before falling below the applicable threshold.

Classes you need to attend consecutively to recover above a threshold.

Possible presentation:

Operating Systems
21 / 25
84%

Status: Safe

You may miss:
1 of the next classes while remaining >= configured threshold

or:

Machine Learning
18 / 24
75%

Need:
X consecutive attended classes to reach Y%

IMPORTANT:

Verify official attendance requirements before labeling anything "safe", "shortage", "eligible", etc.

If rules vary, expose assumptions.

The extension must not claim official exam eligibility based solely on its own calculation.

Use wording such as:

"Estimated from SIS attendance data."

---

# 2. ATTENDANCE WHAT-IF CALCULATOR

Allow:

"If I miss tomorrow's lecture?"

"If I attend the next 5?"

Update percentage instantly.

Example:

Current:
18/22 = 81.8%

Miss next:
18/23 = 78.3%

Attend next 3:
21/25 = 84%

This could be extremely useful.

---

Do not scatter tools randomly across the portal.

Determine the best implementation based on the current Level 2 architecture.

Possible UX patterns:

- dashboard widgets
- companion panel
- Tools section
- contextual buttons within existing pages
- command palette
- modal tools

Use the right surface for each feature.

Do NOT make every feature a floating popup.

---

# CONTEXTUAL FEATURES ARE PREFERRED

A major Level 3 principle:

PUT TOOLS WHERE THEY ARE USEFUL.

Examples:

On Attendance page:

[Attendance Calculator]

On Results page:

[Analyze GPA]

On Current Marks page:

[Grade Projection]

On Timetable:

[Find Empty Room]

On Dashboard:

[Today's Classes]
[Academic Snapshot]

On Transcript:

[CGPA Analysis]

This is much better than putting everything inside one giant tools menu.

---

# BUILD A SHARED DATA LAYER

Level 3 will need information from multiple SIS pages.

Do NOT have every feature independently scrape random DOM elements.

Create a normalized SIS data layer.

Conceptually:

SIS DOM / Pages
        ↓
Portal Adapters
        ↓
Normalized Models
        ↓
Student Companion Services
        ↓
Features / UI

Possible normalized models:

Student
Semester
Course
Enrollment
AttendanceRecord
Assessment
Result
TranscriptEntry
TimetableEntry
FeeRecord

Actual models must be based on real SIS data.

---

# PORTAL DATA CACHE

Some information may exist only on specific pages.

If helpful, cache normalized non-sensitive derived information locally using chrome.storage.

Examples:

- course names
- credit hours
- timetable
- user UI preferences

Be conservative with sensitive academic information.

Prefer session memory when persistent storage provides little benefit.

If persistent academic data is stored:

- keep it local
- document what is stored
- provide a clear-data option
- never upload it anywhere

---

# DATA FRESHNESS

Never let cached information silently appear authoritative when outdated.

Track timestamps.

Example:

Attendance
84%
Updated from SIS 12 minutes ago

Or refresh it when the student visits that page.

Design sensible invalidation.

---

# DO NOT SCRAPE SIS AGGRESSIVELY

Do NOT create background crawlers repeatedly requesting every SIS page.

Prefer:

1. Data already visible
2. Data loaded during normal navigation
3. Carefully requested pages only when genuinely necessary and safe

Avoid generating unnecessary load on university infrastructure.

---

# PRIVACY FIRST

The extension handles educational information.

All Level 3 features should operate locally wherever possible.

DO NOT transmit:

- student name
- roll number
- marks
- attendance
- grades
- CGPA
- transcript
- fees
- timetable
- session cookies
- portal HTML

to our own server or third parties unless I explicitly approve a future feature requiring it.

For this implementation:

ASSUME LOCAL-ONLY PROCESSING.

---

# NO CREDENTIAL HANDLING

Never:

- capture passwords
- store passwords
- export cookies
- log authorization tokens
- inspect credentials for convenience
- create alternate authentication

Authentication remains entirely handled by SIS.

---

# COMSATS PLUS PRIVACY

Do not send the student's SIS information to COMSATS Plus.

The GPA functionality should run locally inside OUR extension.

The Room Finder should not leak student identity or academic information.

If public data must be fetched, request only the public information required for room availability.

---

# DEPENDENCY ON COMSATS PLUS

Try to avoid making critical extension functionality completely dependent on another student's website remaining online forever.

For GPA:

Implement the verified calculation logic ourselves.

Do NOT iframe or embed their calculator.

For Room Finder:

Research the underlying data source.

If availability can reasonably be calculated independently from public timetable data, prefer that architecture.

If an external public data source is genuinely necessary, isolate it behind an adapter so it can be replaced later.

Conceptually:

RoomAvailabilityProvider

instead of:

random fetch() calls spread across components.

---

# ACADEMIC CALCULATION ENGINE

Make academic calculations pure and testable.

Examples:

calculateSemesterGPA()
calculateCGPA()
calculateRequiredGPA()
calculateProjectedCGPA()
calculateAttendancePercentage()
calculateMissableClasses()
calculateRequiredAttendance()
calculateRequiredMarks()
mapPercentageToGrade()

Do not couple mathematical calculations directly to React components or DOM parsing.

---

# UNIT TEST THE IMPORTANT MATH

Add tests for calculation logic.

Test:

- zero credits
- missing courses
- 4.0 GPA
- failing grades
- decimal credit situations if valid
- invalid values
- impossible target CGPA
- target already achieved
- boundary percentages
- grade boundary transitions
- attendance boundary values

Academic tools lose credibility immediately if calculations are wrong.

---

# EXPLAIN CALCULATIONS

When useful, allow students to understand HOW a result was calculated.

For example:

Projected CGPA

Current:
3.28 × 72 credits

Current semester:
3.67 × 18 credits

Projected:
(3.28×72 + 3.67×18) / 90
= 3.36

This builds trust.

---

# UI QUALITY

Level 3 must match the already successful Level 2 visual system.

Do NOT create tools that look like a separate application.

Reuse:

- design tokens
- colors
- dark mode
- spacing
- typography
- cards
- buttons
- inputs
- dialogs
- animations
- border radius

Everything should feel native to our enhanced SIS.

---

# DARK MODE

Every new Level 3 interface must work perfectly in:

- Light
- Dark
- System

No white calculator modals inside dark mode.

No unthemed charts.

No hard-coded text colors.

---

# VISUALIZATIONS

Use visualization only where it adds understanding.

Good:

CGPA trend
Attendance progress
Grade distribution

Bad:

random pie charts everywhere.

Prefer simple readable visuals.

Charts must work in dark mode and remain accessible.

---

# PERFORMANCE

Do not turn the extension into a heavy application.

Avoid:

- continuously running DOM scans
- excessive MutationObservers
- unnecessary polling
- massive chart libraries for tiny visuals
- fetching all SIS pages every load
- duplicated parsers
- excessive dependencies

Level 3 should still feel instant.

---

# RESILIENCE

SIS is an external portal that may change.

All Level 3 enhancements must degrade gracefully.

If a parser fails:

- original SIS continues functioning
- other tools continue functioning
- only affected enhancement disables itself
- development warning is logged

Never let one failed selector break the portal.

---

# FEATURE FLAGS

For substantial features, consider internal feature flags:

studentCompanion.gpa
studentCompanion.roomFinder
studentCompanion.attendance
studentCompanion.courseAnalysis
studentCompanion.commandPalette

This will make future maintenance easier.

Do not overengineer if the existing extension already has an appropriate mechanism.

---

# IMPORTANT UX RULE

Do not dump all possible insights onto the dashboard.

The dashboard should answer:

"What matters right now?"

Examples:

- next class
- today timetable
- attendance warning
- recent marks
- current CGPA
- upcoming relevant item
- find room during free period

Detailed analysis belongs deeper inside relevant pages/tools.

---

# PRIORITIZATION FRAMEWORK

For every potential Level 3 feature ask:

UTILITY
Would students actually use this?

RELIABILITY
Can it be calculated accurately?

DATA
Does SIS provide enough information?

FRICTION
Does it save clicks/time/manual calculation?

PLACEMENT
Where would the student naturally expect it?

MAINTAINABILITY
Will this survive reasonable SIS changes?

PRIVACY
Can it remain local?

Only implement features with strong answers.

---

# REQUIRED CORE FEATURES

Regardless of additional discoveries, Level 3 must include:

1. COMSATS-aware GPA calculator
2. CGPA calculator
3. Target CGPA planner
4. GPA scenario planning
5. Integration with SIS course/credit information where available
6. Academic analysis from current marks where reliable
7. Empty Room Finder
8. Timetable + Room Finder integration where possible
9. At least several genuinely useful portal-native student companion improvements discovered through the SIS audit
10. Clean integration into the Level 2 experience

---

# DO NOT CLONE COMSATS PLUS

We are NOT trying to create:

"COMSATS Plus inside SIS."

We are building:

"A complete student companion built directly into SIS."

COMSATS Plus is being researched specifically because it has useful ideas around:

- GPA tooling
- empty-room discovery

Our extension should go further by taking advantage of authenticated SIS context.

That is our biggest advantage.

For example:

Generic GPA website:

User manually enters:
6 courses
6 grades
6 credit hours

Our extension:

Courses + credit hours automatically loaded from SIS.

Student only changes hypothetical grades.

That is materially better.

---

# DO NOT OVERBUILD NOVELTY FEATURES

Do not implement:

- social network
- chat
- professor ratings
- memory maps
- AI chatbot
- random gamification

unless there is an exceptionally strong reason discovered during the audit.

This Level 3 should focus on:

ACADEMICS
CAMPUS UTILITY
PRODUCTIVITY
PORTAL INTELLIGENCE

---

# IMPLEMENTATION PROCESS

Follow this order.

## STEP 1 — Existing Extension Audit

Understand Level 1 + Level 2 completely.

Do not regress them.

## STEP 2 — Full SIS Reconnaissance

Using Chrome DevTools MCP, manually navigate every meaningful authenticated page.

I will handle login.

Create your internal portal/data map.

## STEP 3 — COMSATS Plus Research

Study:

GPA tools
CGPA tools
planning calculator
internal marks behavior
Empty Room Finder

Determine concepts and data requirements.

## STEP 4 — Official Policy Verification

Research current official COMSATS grading/attendance rules relevant to the calculations.

Never rely only on COMSATS Plus.

## STEP 5 — Feature Opportunity Analysis

Based on the actual portal, decide which additional student-companion features genuinely add value.

## STEP 6 — Architecture

Design:

parsers
normalized models
calculation services
room provider
feature modules
UI integration

Avoid unnecessary rewrite.

## STEP 7 — Implement Core Academic Toolkit

GPA
CGPA
target planner
scenario planner
marks intelligence

# CALCULATION VALIDATION

For every academic calculator:

Compare multiple manually calculated test cases.

Check exact boundary conditions.

Cross-check against official COMSATS policy.

Where appropriate, compare results against COMSATS Plus as an additional sanity check.

If results disagree:

DO NOT arbitrarily choose one.

Investigate why.

Official CUI policy and the student's applicable academic cohort take precedence.

---

# ROOM FINDER VALIDATION

Verify several cases manually:

Room marked free → confirm timetable has no class in that period.

Room marked occupied → confirm scheduled class.

Boundary between time slots.

Current-time transitions.

Different days.

Long free periods.

Labs.

Special rooms if present.

Do not call it "real-time" unless the underlying data genuinely provides real-time occupancy.

If it is timetable-derived, label it appropriately, for example:

"Available according to timetable."

Accuracy in wording matters.

---

# SECURITY REVIEW

Before finishing confirm:

No passwords handled.
No cookies exported.
No student data transmitted.
No unnecessary host permissions.
No undocumented destructive requests.
No modification of SIS records.
No excessive portal requests.
No external analytics containing academic data.

---

# FINAL PRODUCT STANDARD

Level 2 made SIS beautiful.

Level 3 must make SIS intelligent.

The final experience should feel like:

SIS
+
Academic Planner
+
Attendance Assistant
+
GPA Analyzer
+
Timetable Assistant
+
Campus Room Finder
+
Student Productivity Layer

all integrated seamlessly into one portal.

A student should be able to open SIS and quickly answer questions like:

"What class do I have next?"

"Where can I sit during my break?"

"What is my attendance situation?"

"What happens if I miss another class?"

"What GPA am I heading toward?"

"What grades do I need for a 3.5?"

"What marks do I need in the final?"

"How has my CGPA changed?"

"Where are my marks?"

"What should I pay attention to today?"

without navigating through half a dozen disconnected pages or manually calculating things.

Use the actual portal to discover additional questions we can answer.

That is the goal of Level 3.

Make autonomous engineering and UX decisions where the evidence is clear.

Do not repeatedly ask me trivial implementation questions.

Inspect the application, understand the data, choose the best implementation, build it, test it, and polish it.

Most importantly:

PRESERVE LEVEL 1.
PRESERVE LEVEL 2.
KEEP SIS FUNCTIONAL.
KEEP STUDENT DATA PRIVATE.
VERIFY ACADEMIC RULES.
DO NOT FABRICATE DATA.
DISTINGUISH PROJECTIONS FROM OFFICIAL RESULTS.
MAKE EVERY FEATURE GENUINELY USEFUL.
